title: Nivolumab + ipilimumab · colorectal after chemotherapy
purpose: These two immunotherapy medicines aim to control bowel cancer with a confirmed MSI-H/dMMR DNA-repair feature. This pathway follows previous fluoropyrimidine-based combination chemotherapy.
context_label: MSI-H/dMMR metastatic colorectal cancer after fluoropyrimidine-based combination chemotherapy
indication_text: MSI-H/dMMR metastatic colorectal cancer after fluoropyrimidine-based combination chemotherapy
schedule_summary: Cycles 1–4: nivolumab 3 mg/kg, then ipilimumab 1 mg/kg, on Day 1 every 21 days. The first nivolumab-only dose is due three weeks after the final combination dose, subject to clinical review. Nivolumab alone: 240 mg IV or 600 mg under the skin every two weeks, or 1200 mg under the skin every four weeks.
administration_text: During the first four cycles, nivolumab is infused first over about 30 minutes, then ipilimumab over about 30 minutes. Allow extra time for checks and observation. Nivolumab alone: 240 mg IV or 600 mg under the skin every two weeks, or 1200 mg under the skin every four weeks.
monitoring_summary: Before starting and before every cycle: blood count, kidney and liver profile, glucose and thyroid function. Cortisol is checked if clinically indicated. Disease assessment follows the consultant plan. Continue monitoring for late immune effects for at least five months after the final dose.

agents.name: Nivolumab
agents.explanation: Nivolumab blocks PD-1, a brake on immune T cells. This can help immune cells attack cancer, but can also inflame healthy organs.
agents.watch: Report new breathing, bowel, hormone, skin, heart or nerve symptoms promptly.
risks: Immune inflammation of lungs, bowel, liver, kidneys, glands, skin, heart, nerves or muscles
Infusion reactions; injection-site effects if given under the skin
Some effects need hospital treatment, steroids or long-term hormone replacement
Effects can begin after the final dose

agents.name: Ipilimumab
agents.explanation: Ipilimumab blocks another immune brake, CTLA-4, helping activate T cells. Combining two immune medicines can increase anti-cancer activity and also the risk of serious immune inflammation.
agents.watch: Report diarrhoea, abdominal pain, skin changes, headache, weakness or other new symptoms immediately.
risks: Immune liver, hormone, skin, nervous-system and other organ inflammation
Some adverse effects persist after the four-dose phase

urgent_extra: Contact oncology immediately for new breathlessness, persistent diarrhoea, severe tummy pain, yellow skin or eyes, much less urine, spreading or blistering rash, severe headache, marked weakness, confusion, unusual thirst or passing much more urine. Severe breathing difficulty, chest pain, collapse or seizure needs emergency care. Effects can begin after treatment ends.
consent_support: Discuss the exact colorectal setting and two treatment phases, expected benefit and uncertainty, alternatives, greater immune-toxicity risk with the combination, possible hospital care, steroids, lasting hormone replacement and rare life-threatening effects. Explain late toxicity, pregnancy precautions, the contact plan and the option to reconsider.
safety_note: Immune effects can happen on any day and after treatment ends. Carry your immunotherapy alert card and tell every healthcare team that you have received nivolumab and ipilimumab.

chronology_notes.text: Cycles 1–4: nivolumab 3 mg/kg, then ipilimumab 1 mg/kg, on Day 1 every 21 days. The first nivolumab-only dose is due three weeks after the final combination dose, subject to clinical review. Nivolumab alone: 240 mg IV or 600 mg under the skin every two weeks, or 1200 mg under the skin every four weeks.

chronology_notes.title: The first maintenance visit

chronology_notes.title: Late immune effects

timeline_note: This 21-day calendar describes the first four combination cycles. Maintenance uses the separately confirmed two- or four-week schedule.

phases.label: Cycles 1–4: two immunotherapies
phases.detail: Nivolumab 3 mg/kg followed by ipilimumab 1 mg/kg on Day 1. Both are given as infusions. The first nivolumab-only dose is due three weeks after the final combination dose, subject to clinical review.

phases.label: Cycle 5 onwards: nivolumab alone
phases.detail: Nivolumab alone: 240 mg IV or 600 mg under the skin every two weeks, or 1200 mg under the skin every four weeks. Continue while helping and tolerable, until progression or unacceptable toxicity. This colorectal regimen does not set a fixed overall two-year limit.

day_groups.title: Combination visit: cycles 1–4
day_groups.body: Blood results and symptoms are reviewed. Nivolumab is given first, then ipilimumab. The team monitors you during treatment and afterwards.
day_groups.action: Tell the nurse immediately if you become itchy, flushed, breathless, dizzy or suddenly unwell.

day_groups.title: Between combination visits
day_groups.body: Immune inflammation can begin at any time; the calendar cannot predict a safe symptom-free week.
day_groups.action: After cycle 4, confirm the nivolumab-only dose, route, interval and first maintenance date.

support.title: Sickness prevention and premedication
support.text: Nivolumab has minimal and ipilimumab low emetogenic potential. Routine premedication is not usually required; the team individualises anti-sickness treatment and care after any previous reaction.

support.title: Steroids and other treatment for immune effects
support.text: Do not self-start or stop steroids. If prescribed, follow the exact taper and any infection-prevention plan. Do not restart cancer treatment until the team explicitly authorises it. If the team changes the interval between nivolumab-only doses, they will give you a new appointment plan: the first four-weekly dose is two weeks after the last two-weekly dose, or the first two-weekly dose is four weeks after the last four-weekly dose. Do not change the schedule yourself. This does not change which formulations are permitted for your colorectal treatment.

support.title: Pregnancy and feeding
support.text: Discuss fertility and effective contraception before treatment. Effective contraception continues for at least five months after the last nivolumab dose. Do not breastfeed during treatment; agree any later feeding plan with the team.

anatomy: New severe headache, dizziness, confusion, weakness, thirst or extra urine needs urgent advice; hormone effects may need long-term treatment.
New cough or breathlessness can signal inflammation or another urgent cause.
Chest pain, racing heartbeat or fainting needs urgent assessment.
Yellow eyes/skin or dark urine may signal inflammation; tests also check the liver.
Report much less urine, new swelling or a change in kidney tests.
New or persistent diarrhoea, blood in stools or severe tummy pain needs urgent advice.
Spreading rash, blisters, severe weakness or muscle pain needs prompt review.
Report eye pain or new visual change promptly; do not wait for the next cycle.

evidence.title: Evidence for this colorectal setting
evidence.intro: CheckMate 142 followed 119 previously treated people receiving nivolumab 3 mg/kg plus ipilimumab 1 mg/kg, followed by nivolumab alone.
evidence.population: MSI-H/dMMR metastatic colorectal cancer after fluoropyrimidine-based combination chemotherapy
evidence.interpretation: The four-year follow-up reported sustained responses in this single-arm cohort. Without a randomised control group, it cannot establish how much longer a person lives compared with another treatment.
evidence.limitations: This was a previously treated cohort and used intravenous nivolumab maintenance. First-line CheckMate 8HW and subcutaneous formulations are different evidence questions.

chapters.title: Your cancer and treatment aim
chapters.intro: A validated tumour result helps select this treatment.

items.title: MSI-H and dMMR
items.text: These describe a feature of the cancer’s DNA-repair system. The result helps identify colorectal cancers that may respond to immunotherapy. Ask whether a genetics assessment is relevant.

items.title: Your treatment setting
items.text: These two immunotherapy medicines aim to control bowel cancer with a confirmed MSI-H/dMMR DNA-repair feature. This pathway follows previous fluoropyrimidine-based combination chemotherapy.

items.title: Choices and goals
items.text: Discuss the likely benefit, uncertainty, other treatment options, clinical trials and symptom-focused care in relation to your priorities.

chapters.title: How the two medicines work
chapters.intro: They act at two different immune-control points.

items.title: Nivolumab
items.text: Nivolumab blocks PD-1, a brake on immune T cells. This can help immune cells attack cancer, but can also inflame healthy organs.

items.title: Ipilimumab
items.text: Ipilimumab blocks another immune brake, CTLA-4, helping activate T cells. Combining two immune medicines can increase anti-cancer activity and also the risk of serious immune inflammation.

items.title: Why side effects need prompt assessment
items.text: Immune activity may inflame healthy organs. The combination can cause serious effects, and symptoms may continue or begin after ipilimumab or all treatment stops. Pauses, steroids or permanent discontinuation may be needed.

chapters.title: Combination first, then nivolumab alone
chapters.intro: Keep both phases in your written plan.

items.title: Four combination cycles
items.text: Nivolumab 3 mg/kg and ipilimumab 1 mg/kg are given on Day 1 every 21 days for four cycles. Nivolumab is infused first, then ipilimumab; each infusion takes about 30 minutes, with additional preparation and observation.

items.title: First nivolumab-only treatment
items.text: The first nivolumab-only dose is due three weeks after the final combination dose, subject to clinical review.

items.title: Maintenance options
items.text: Nivolumab alone: 240 mg IV or 600 mg under the skin every two weeks, or 1200 mg under the skin every four weeks.

items.title: How long treatment continues
items.text: Continue while helping and tolerable, until progression or unacceptable toxicity. This colorectal regimen does not set a fixed overall two-year limit.

items.title: Under-the-skin maintenance
items.text: The team may select the specific nivolumab formulation given under the skin over about 3–5 minutes. Tell staff about sore, red or bruised skin at the injection site. Dose and route must match the prescription; they are not interchangeable by simple volume.

items.title: Changing maintenance appointments
items.text: If the team changes the interval between nivolumab-only doses, they will give you a new appointment plan: the first four-weekly dose is two weeks after the last two-weekly dose, or the first two-weekly dose is four weeks after the last four-weekly dose. Do not change the schedule yourself. This does not change which formulations are permitted for your colorectal treatment.

items.title: Blood and thyroid tests
items.text: Before starting and before every cycle: blood count, kidney and liver profile, glucose and thyroid function. Cortisol is checked if clinically indicated. Disease assessment follows the consultant plan. Continue monitoring for late immune effects for at least five months after the final dose.

items.title: Scans and markers
items.text: The supervising consultant determines imaging, tumour-marker and other disease-monitoring tests. Ask when each test is due and who will review the result.

items.title: Treatment delays
items.text: If a dose is held, the team decides whether and when either medicine can restart. Do not assume one medicine is safe to receive when the other has been withheld.

items.title: Bowels and hydration
items.text: Report new diarrhoea, blood in stools or abdominal pain immediately. Immune bowel inflammation can worsen and needs assessment; do not rely on self-treatment alone.

items.title: Energy, hormones and daily life
items.text: New marked fatigue, headache, dizziness, weakness, thirst or extra urine can need hormone/glucose tests. Ask for help with eating, activity, sleep, work and caring responsibilities.

items.title: Medicine list and steroids
items.text: Tell the team about all medicines, supplements and steroid use. Follow any steroid taper exactly and carry information about hormone replacement.

items.title: Pregnancy and feeding
items.text: Discuss fertility and effective contraception before treatment. Effective contraception continues for at least five months after the last nivolumab dose. Do not breastfeed during treatment; agree any later feeding plan with the team.

chapters.title: Urgent symptoms and care after treatment
chapters.intro: Do not wait for the next appointment.

items.title: What to report
items.text: Contact oncology immediately for new breathlessness, persistent diarrhoea, severe tummy pain, yellow skin or eyes, much less urine, spreading or blistering rash, severe headache, marked weakness, confusion, unusual thirst or passing much more urine. Severe breathing difficulty, chest pain, collapse or seizure needs emergency care. Effects can begin after treatment ends.

items.title: During infusions
items.text: Alert the nurse immediately if you feel itchy, flushed, breathless, dizzy, tight-chested or suddenly unwell.

items.title: Late effects
items.text: Keep the alert card and report symptoms after treatment stops. NCCP specifies continuous monitoring for at least five months after the last dose. Some hormone changes need longer follow-up.
